newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA confirms to advise Thailand on baht float.
newsitem.headline: RBA confirms to advise Thailand on baht float.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) would provide technical advice to the Bank of Thailand in the managed float of the Thai baht, an RBA spokesman confirmed.
"We've been asked and we will provide," the spokesman said, adding that a senior bank officer would fly to Thailand soon.
Earlier, the Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said Thailand had sought technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund and the RBA.
The Australian dollar was floated in December 1993.
So far, the central bank has only intervened in extreme movements of the Australian dollar and says it does not target a particular level for the dollar.

The last time the central bank noticeably intervened in Australian dollar trading was in 1993 when the local dollar fell to a low around 64 U.S. cents due to uncertainty surrounding the government's budget legislation, which was held up in parliament.
RBA governor Ian Macfarlane is a strong proponent of greater central bank co-operation and has repeatedly called for the establishment of an Asian Bank of International Settlements.
The RBA currently prints the Thai baht and other foreign banknote at its plant in Melbourne.
A spokesman for the RBA later said it not been determined yet who the central bank would send to Thailand to provide expertise and for how long that staff member would be staying.
"We will be providing technical assistance by making available one of our staff," he said.
